title: Diagnose the core challenge
summary: Good strategy names the main obstacle in the way. A clear diagnosis tells you where to focus, and stops the strategy becoming a list of goals.

beginner: From your summary, list the problems that hold the product or company back.
Ask which one, if solved, would make the others easier.
Write it as a short diagnosis: what is going on and why it matters.
Check it with two or three people who know the area well.
Keep goals and wishes out of the diagnosis.
intermediate: Look for root causes rather than symptoms.
Test the diagnosis against evidence that could prove it wrong.
Agree the diagnosis with the sponsor before choosing what to do.
experienced: Diagnose across products or teams, where the real challenge often sits.
Name uncomfortable causes, such as how the organisation works.
Use the diagnosis to rule out popular but weak options.

toolExamples.miro: Group problems and draw how they cause each other.
toolExamples.confluence: Publish the diagnosis as a short page for comment.

pitfalls: Writing goals instead of a diagnosis

sources.title: The perils of bad strategy (Richard Rumelt, McKinsey Quarterly)
